extracted.intended_audience: students/readers of classical Euclidean geometry (learners of geometric constructions)
extracted.subtask_description: Classical Euclidean-style constructions and propositions showing how to divide triangles, parallelograms, quadrilaterals and lines into equal parts (areas or segments) using diameters, parallels, midpoints and proportional lengths; also classification of quadrilaterals and relationships between square-on-line and area operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide a triangle into two equal parts
rubrics_metrics.description: To divide a given triangle into two equal parts (areas) by a line: draw from a vertex to the opposite side (or appropriate point) so that the triangle is cut into two parts equal in area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the line from the chosen vertex to the midpoint (or a suitably determined point) of the opposite side. The text demonstrates procedures and numerical examples showing how to choose the point on the side (often by proportional multiplication or taking the 'mita' / half) so that the resulting two parts are equal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide a triangle into three (or more) equal parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct lines which divide a triangle into three equal-area parts by drawing lines from a vertex (or from points) so that the triangle is partitioned into three equal areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method uses dividing a side (or a line through the triangle) into equal parts and drawing corresponding lines (often parallel to a base) so that similar triangles or equal-area strips result. The text gives stepwise constructions (divide side into 3 parts, draw lines accordingly) and arithmetic examples showing proportional multiplications to locate the division points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide a triangle into n equal parts via parallels / proportional segments
rubrics_metrics.description: To divide a triangle into n equal area parts by drawing lines parallel to one side at distances proportional to the square roots or linear proportions dictated by similar triangles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the similarity of triangles: divide the altitude or a base into proportional segments (often by multiplying lengths) so that lines drawn parallel to a side cut off equal areas. The text supplies numerical multiplications and square-root reasoning to compute the needed proportional distances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide a triangle using an interior or given point
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a point in or on a triangle (e.g., a point on a side or interior), construct a line through that point which divides the triangle into specified equal parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures include drawing auxiliary lines (to vertices or along parallels), using the given point to mark equal-area strips or to create equal subdivisions via parallels, and using proportions computed by multiplication of segment lengths as illustrated in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of quadrilaterals into four species
rubrics_metrics.description: Quadrilaterals are classified into types: (1) parallelograms, (2) rectangles (or quadrilaterals with right angles), (3) long-sided ones with opposite sides equal and not right angles, (4) rhomboids (sides opposite equal but angles unequal) — described by their side equalities and angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text enumerates these species, explains defining properties (opposite sides equal, right angles or not), and how to recognize them in figures. This classification underpins subsequent constructions and equal-area arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide a quadrilateral into two equal parts through a given point
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a quadrilateral and a specified point (on or inside it), construct a line through that point which divides the quadrilateral into two equal-area parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple constructions are given: draw diameters or diagonals, use parallels equidistant to given sides, or construct lines equidistant to pairs of sides so that resulting subfigures are equal. The text shows how to choose and use diameters (e.g., draw diameter a–c or b–d) and equidistant lines to achieve equal-area partitioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide a parallelogram (or parallel-sided figure) into equal parts by equidistant lines
rubrics_metrics.description: To cut a parallelogram or regions bounded by parallels into n equal parts, draw lines equidistant and parallel to a side (or through specified points) to produce equal area strips or congruent parallelograms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method: mark off equal divisions along one side or along a diameter and draw lines parallel to the opposite side; the text gives examples of dividing into 2, 3, 4, or more equal parts and shows how equidistant parallel lines produce equal areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using diameters and intersections to create equal-area subdivisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use diameters (diagonals or lines joining opposite vertices) and their intersections with suitably drawn lines to partition quadrilaterals into equal parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples instruct drawing diameters (e.g., a–c) and then constructing lines through intersection points so that the quadrilateral is cut into parts equal to triangles or other quadrilaterals; the constructions rely on symmetry and equalities produced by the chosen diameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: If lines are equidistant, corresponding bounded figures are equal
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines (or strips) that are equidistant and bounded by the same parallels (or same end-lines) produce areas equal to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle is repeatedly used: construct lines equidistant from given sides so that the strips (rectangles, parallelograms, or trapezoids) between them have equal area. The text applies this to build equal subdivisions and to compare areas across figures bounded by equidistant lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide a given line segment into n equal parts
rubrics_metrics.description: To divide a given straight line into n equal segments by using parallels and proportional constructions from auxiliary lines or points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: from an endpoint draw an auxiliary ray and mark off n equal segments on it; join the last mark to the opposite endpoint of the given line and draw parallels through the other marks to that joining line to obtain equal divisions on the original segment. Text refers to dividing into 2, 3, 4, etc., parts and demonstrates with figures and numeric examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct equal-area figures by composing/splitting into triangles and squares
rubrics_metrics.description: Create or compare areas by decomposing quadrilaterals into triangles or squares on sides; equal triangles or squares produce equal areas when arranged or compared appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text shows composing figures (e.g., quadrilateral as sum of triangles), producing equal triangles by drawing parallels or cutting off equal parts, and using squares on lines (area of square built on a segment) to reason about area multiplications and roots with numerical examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate squares on lines to areas and use multiplication / roots for proportional constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use arithmetic relations of squares (square of a line) and multiplication to determine lengths needed to produce equal areas (including use of roots when reversing from area to length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book gives numeric examples: multiplying lengths, forming squares on lines, taking square-roots, and using those computations to scale constructions (e.g., when dividing areas proportionally or when computing distances for parallel cuts). It demonstrates transforming area-requirements into proportional length constructions via multiplication and root extraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of similar triangles and proportionality to locate division points
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ similarity of triangles and proportional segments to determine where on a side (or altitude) to draw a line so that the cut produces the desired area ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many constructions rely on creating similar triangles by drawing parallels; then proportions between sides determine areas of the strips/triangles. The text walks through forming the similar triangles and computing the required proportions by multiplication to obtain exact division points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide polygons by composing congruent/paired triangles or quadrilaterals
rubrics_metrics.description: Partition a polygon (especially quadrilateral) into congruent triangles or congruent quadrilaterals so that combining those building blocks produces equal-area subdivisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The techniques include erecting lines from vertices to produce sets of congruent triangles (by equal bases and equal heights via parallels) and then aggregating them to form halves, thirds, etc., of the original polygon. The text gives stepwise compositions and multiple illustrative cases.
